name: Downtown Halifax
tagline: Waterfront boardwalk, offices and the pub scene
description: Downtown runs from the Citadel hill down steep streets to a long wooden harbour boardwalk lined with breweries, seafood shacks and ferry terminals. Argyle and Barrington streets hold the pubs, live music venues and most of the city's coworking spaces. The population is young professionals in newer glass rentals mixed with students.
bestFor: Nomads who want to walk to a coworking desk, a pub and the ferry without owning a car.
pros: Coworking spaces and cafes concentrated here
Harbour boardwalk and ferry on the doorstep
cons: Bar noise on Argyle Street until 2am
Steep hills and brutal wind off the harbour in winter

name: North End
tagline: Gentrified creative quarter on Agricola Street
description: The North End is Halifax's most changed district, where Agricola and Gottingen streets now hold third-wave coffee roasters, breweries, tattoo studios and independent restaurants among older wooden houses. It has the city's strongest creative and startup crowd plus the Hydrostone market block. Rents rose fast but still sit below downtown.
bestFor: Nomads who want good coffee, indie restaurants and a design or startup crowd nearby.
pros: Best independent cafe and brewery scene in the city
20 minute walk or short bus to downtown
Character housing with decent value flats
cons: Gentrification is uneven, some blocks feel rough at night
Older wooden houses can be poorly insulated
Street parking is scarce and permit controlled

name: South End
tagline: Leafy university streets and grand old houses
description: The South End holds Dalhousie and Saint Mary's universities, Point Pleasant Park at the peninsula tip and streets of large Victorian houses under mature trees. It is quiet, safe and green, with student flats mixed into wealthier family blocks. Spring Garden Road provides the shops and cafes at its northern edge.
bestFor: Remote workers who want quiet streets, a big park and a walk to downtown.
pros: Point Pleasant Park trails right at the end of the peninsula
Walk to downtown in 20 minutes along Spring Garden
cons: Expensive, and good flats go fast each September
Student turnover makes some blocks noisy in term time
Few restaurants once you leave Spring Garden Road

name: West End and Quinpool
tagline: Family streets with a practical high street
description: The West End sits between the Common and the Northwest Arm, centred on Quinpool Road with its grocery stores, gyms, pharmacies and a long run of cheap ethnic restaurants. Behind it are quiet residential streets of duplexes and family homes near Chebucto and the Arm. It is the most practical everyday part of the peninsula.
bestFor: Longer stays where groceries, a gym and a quiet desk matter more than nightlife.
pros: Everyday shops and groceries all on one street
Cheaper than downtown but still on the peninsula
Quiet at night, good for early calls
cons: Limited nightlife, you head downtown for evenings
Quinpool Road traffic is heavy at rush hour
Older rental stock with dated kitchens

name: Downtown Dartmouth
tagline: Cheaper side of the harbour with the best skyline view
description: Downtown Dartmouth faces Halifax across the harbour, reached by a 12 minute passenger ferry with the best skyline view in the region. Portland Street has grown a solid run of cafes, breweries and restaurants, and the Dartmouth lakes offer swimming and paddling in summer. Rents run clearly below the Halifax peninsula.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads happy to take a ferry commute for lower rent and lake swimming.
pros: Noticeably cheaper rents than the Halifax side
Ferry ride into downtown takes 12 minutes
cons: Ferry stops running late at night, then it is a long bus
Fewer coworking options than Halifax proper
Pockets outside the core still feel neglected
